items.prose: Three partners put £12,000, £16,000 and £32,000 into a business. They share each year's profit in the ratio of what they put in.

parts.question: In its simplest form, how many parts does the ratio $12{,}000 : 16{,}000 : 32{,}000$ have in all?

feedback.correct: Each amount divides by 4,000, so the ratio is $3 : 4 : 8$, which has $3 + 4 + 8 = 15$ parts.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide each amount by the largest number that goes into all three.

byKey.thousands: You divided by 1,000 only, giving $12 : 16 : 32$. All three still share a factor of 4.
byKey.halved: You divided by 2,000, giving $6 : 8 : 16$. All three still share a factor of 2.

explain.text: 4,000 divides all three amounts: $3 : 4 : 8$. Nothing else divides 3, 4 and 8, so this is the simplest form. It has 15 parts.

parts.question: Using 15 parts, the first year's profit is £9,600. How much does the partner who put in £32,000 receive, in pounds?

feedback.correct: One part is $9{,}600 \div 15 = 640$, and this partner has 8 parts: $8 \times 640 = 5{,}120$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find one part, then multiply by this partner's number of parts.

byKey.equal: You split the profit equally. The partners share in the ratio $3 : 4 : 8$, so this one gets 8 parts.
byKey.one-part: That is one part. The £32,000 partner has 8 parts: £5,120.

explain.text: One part is $9{,}600 \div 15 = 640$ pounds. The partner who put in £32,000 holds 8 parts, so receives £5,120.

parts.question: The next year, the partner who put in £12,000 receives £2,850. Using the ratio $3 : 4 : 8$, what was that year's total profit, in pounds?

feedback.correct: 3 parts are £2,850, so one part is £950 and 15 parts are $15 \times 950 = 14{,}250$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. The £2,850 is 3 parts. Find one part, then the 12 parts of the whole.

byKey.own-parts: You multiplied £2,850 by 3. It is already 3 parts, so divide by 3 to get one part.
byKey.one-part-share: You treated £2,850 as one part. It is the 3 parts of the smallest partner.

explain.text: The smallest partner holds 3 parts, so one part is $2{,}850 \div 3 = 950$ pounds. The whole profit is 15 parts: £14,250.

parts.question: A fourth partner joins with £8,000, so the stakes are now in the ratio $3 : 4 : 8 : 2$. Of an £11,900 profit, how much does the new partner receive, in pounds?

feedback.correct: There are now 17 parts, so one part is $11{,}900 \div 17 = 700$, and 2 parts are £1,400.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the new partner's parts to the total first.

byKey.old-parts: You divided by the old 15 parts. With the new partner there are $3 + 4 + 8 + 2 = 17$.
byKey.equal: You split the profit four ways equally. The new partner holds 2 of the 17 parts.

explain.text: The parts add to $3 + 4 + 8 + 2 = 17$. One part is $11{,}900 \div 17 = 700$ pounds, so the new partner's 2 parts are £1,400.

items.prose: A print shop has an order for 36,000 leaflets. Four identical presses would print the order in 15 hours.

parts.question: How long would 8 presses take? Give your answer in hours as a decimal.

feedback.correct: The order takes $4 \times 15 = 60$ press-hours, so 8 presses take $60 \div 8 = 7.5$ hours.
feedback.generic: Not quite. More presses share the same work, so the time goes down. Find the press-hours first.

byKey.direct: You scaled the time up with the presses. More presses finish sooner: this is inverse proportion.
byKey.subtracted: You took 4 hours off for 4 more presses. Presses times hours stays at 60, so the time is 7.5 hours.

explain.text: Presses times hours is fixed at $4 \times 15 = 60$. With 8 presses the time is $60 \div 8 = 7.5$ hours.

parts.question: Each press costs £14 an hour to run. Using 7.5 hours from part 1, what does the order cost to run on 8 presses, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Multiply presses by hours, then by £14 a press-hour.

byKey.direct: That uses 30 hours, from scaling the time the wrong way. With 7.5 hours the cost is £840.
byKey.one-press: That is one press for 7.5 hours. All 8 presses run: $8 \times 105 = 840$.

explain.text: The order uses $8 \times 7.5 = 60$ press-hours at £14 each, so it costs £840. Four presses for 15 hours also make 60 press-hours, so the cost is the same.

parts.question: Using a cost of £840, what does the shop pay per 1,000 leaflets? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the order in thousands, then divide the cost by that count.

byKey.per-leaflet: That is the cost of one leaflet. Multiply by 1,000, or divide £840 by 36: £23.33.
byKey.upside-down: You divided 36,000 by 840, which gives leaflets per pound. The cost per 1,000 is $840 \div 36$.

explain.text: The order is 36 lots of 1,000 leaflets. $840 \div 36 \approx 23.33$, so each 1,000 costs £23.33 to run.

parts.question: A rival printer quotes £2.20 per 100 leaflets. Using the shop's cost of £23.33 per 1,000, which is the better buy?

options.why: Scale the rival's price first. Per 1,000 it charges $10 \times 2.20 = 22.00$ pounds, which is less than £23.33.
Scale the rival's price to 1,000 leaflets: $10 \times 2.20 = 22.00$, which is less than £23.33.

feedback.correct: Correct. £2.20 per 100 is £22.00 per 1,000, which is £1.33 less than £23.33.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Put both prices on the same unit, 1,000 leaflets.

explain.text: 1,000 leaflets are 10 lots of 100, so the rival charges $10 \times 2.20 = 22.00$ pounds. That beats £23.33. On the whole order it saves $36 \times 1.33 \approx 48$ pounds.

items.prose: A café chain buys coffee beans abroad. A Swiss supplier sells 12 kg for CHF 330 and a German supplier sells 15 kg for €441. The bank quotes £1 = CHF 1.10 and £1 = €1.20.

parts.question: What is the Swiss price per kilogram? Give your answer in francs to 2 decimal places.

widget.label: Swiss price per kg in francs

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide the price by the number of kilograms.

byKey.upside-down: You divided 12 by 330, which gives kilograms per franc. The price per kilogram is $330 \div 12$.
byKey.german: That is the German supplier's price in euros. The Swiss price is $330 \div 12 = 27.50$ francs.

explain.text: A unit price is the total over the amount. $330 \div 12 = 27.50$, so the Swiss beans cost CHF 27.50 a kilogram.

parts.question: Using CHF 27.50 per kilogram, what is the Swiss price per kilogram in pounds? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny.

widget.label: Swiss price per kg in pounds

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each pound buys 1.10 francs, so divide the francs by 1.10.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied by 1.10. A pound buys more than one franc, so there are fewer pounds: divide.

explain.text: The rate gives francs per pound, so pounds are francs divided by 1.10. $27.50 \div 1.10 = 25.00$. Check: $25 \times 1.10 = 27.50$.

parts.question: What is the German price per kilogram in pounds? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny.

widget.label: German price per kg in pounds

feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the euros per kilogram, then divide by 1.20.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied by 1.20. Each pound buys €1.20, so divide: £24.50.
byKey.euros: That is the price in euros. Divide by 1.20 to get pounds: £24.50.

explain.text: The German price is $441 \div 15 = 29.40$ euros a kilogram. Each pound buys €1.20, so it is $29.40 \div 1.20 = 24.50$ pounds.

parts.question: The chain uses 90 kg of beans a month. Using £25.00 and £24.50 per kilogram, what does the cheaper supplier save it each month, in pounds?

feedback.correct: The German beans are £0.50 a kilogram cheaper, and $90 \times 0.50 = 45$, so £45.00 a month.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the saving on one kilogram, then scale it to 90 kg.

byKey.per-kg: That is the saving on one kilogram. The chain buys 90 kg: $90 \times 0.50 = 45$.
byKey.multiplied: That uses £30.25 and £35.28, from multiplying by the rates. With £25.00 and £24.50 the saving is £45.00.

explain.text: The German supplier is $25.00 - 24.50 = 0.50$ pounds a kilogram cheaper. The saving is in direct proportion to the amount bought, so 90 kg save $90 \times 0.50 = 45$ pounds.

items.prose: A group of friends rents a holiday villa in Portugal for a week and shares the euro price. The pound buys €1.125.

parts.question: With 8 friends sharing equally, each pays €405. Two friends drop out. How much does each of the 6 pay now, in euros?

feedback.correct: The villa costs $8 \times 405 = 3{,}240$ euros, so each of 6 pays $3{,}240 \div 6 = 540$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Fewer friends share the same price, so each share goes up.

byKey.direct: You scaled the share down with the people. Fewer people sharing means each pays more: inverse proportion.
byKey.unchanged: The villa's price is fixed, so each share must rise when people drop out.

explain.text: People times share is the villa's price, $8 \times 405 = 3{,}240$ euros. With 6 people each share is $3{,}240 \div 6 = 540$ euros.

parts.question: Using a share of €540, how much is that in pounds? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each pound buys €1.125, so divide the euros by 1.125.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied by 1.125. A pound buys more than one euro, so there are fewer pounds: divide.

explain.text: The rate is euros per pound, so pounds are euros divided by 1.125. $540 \div 1.125 = 480$. Check: $480 \times 1.125 = 540$.

parts.question: The 6 friends change their minds and share the €3,240 by nights stayed. Four friends stay all 7 nights and two stay only 4 nights. How much does a 7-night friend pay, in euros?

feedback.correct: The nights add to $4 \times 7 + 2 \times 4 = 36$, so one night is $3{,}240 \div 36 = 90$ euros and 7 nights are €630.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Count every friend's nights to get the total number of parts.

byKey.equal: That is the equal split. Sharing by nights gives each friend parts in the ratio $7 : 7 : 7 : 7 : 4 : 4$.
byKey.two-parts: You split €3,240 in the ratio $7 : 4$ once. There are four 7-night friends and two 4-night friends: 36 parts.
byKey.four-nights: That is a 4-night friend's share. A 7-night friend pays $7 \times 90 = 630$ euros.

explain.text: The ratio of nights is $7 : 7 : 7 : 7 : 4 : 4$, which is 36 parts. One part is $3{,}240 \div 36 = 90$ euros, so a 7-night friend pays €630.

parts.question: Using €630 by nights and €540 shared equally, how much more does a 7-night friend pay? Give your answer in pounds.

feedback.correct: The extra is $630 - 540 = 90$ euros, and $90 \div 1.125 = 80$ pounds.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the extra in euros, then turn it into pounds.

byKey.euros: That is the extra in euros. Divide by 1.125 to get pounds: £80.00.
byKey.multiplied: You multiplied the €90 by 1.125. To get pounds divide: $90 \div 1.125 = 80$.

explain.text: Sharing by nights costs a 7-night friend $630 - 540 = 90$ euros more. At €1.125 to the pound that is $90 \div 1.125 = 80$ pounds.
